discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, opening neutrino astronomy beyond the Sun and SN 1987A
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived and led IceCube, which turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a neutrino telescope, the culmination of a programme that began with AMANDA. In 2013 IceCube reported a diffuse flux of PeV-scale neutrinos of cosmic origin, the first such detection beyond the Sun and SN 1987A. It followed this with careful statistical work: coincident detection of the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056 (2018), evidence for neutrinos from the active galaxy NGC 1068 (2022), and a map of the Galactic plane in neutrinos (2023). These results opened a new observational window on the most energetic processes in the universe and on the origin of cosmic rays. They also give unique tests of neutrino physics at energies no accelerator can reach. This is a new instrument that created a new field, and its results were built up over a decade with exemplary control of systematics.
